title: Closing the long-range gap: the triangular lattice is not a local minimum of the harmonic zero-point energy for Riesz s = 3 and dipolar potentials, certified with an Ewald split
description:
For a radial pair potential and unit-covolume planar lattices, let E(t) be the harmonic zero-point energy per particle (hbar = m = 1) along the symmetric shear Lt = Pt Lρ that starts at the triangular lattice. An earlier preprint (N2, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23663551) certified E(t) < E(0) for two Yukawa potentials but could not treat r−3 tails, because the real-space lattice sums converge too slowly. Here an Ewald split (a fast-decaying real-space part and a smooth Fourier part) removes the obstacle, and we certify E(t) < E(0) for every 0 < |t| ≤ 10−5 for seven potentials: Riesz r−3; the bilayer point dipole 2(1/r − 1/√(r²+d²))/d² at d = 1/10 and d = 1/2 (N2 covolume units); and at the four preregistered ratios d/a = 0.06, 0.09, 0.1, 0.5. So the triangular lattice is not a local minimum of the model's harmonic zero-point energy over lattice shapes for all seven. The hoped-for first certified positive (local minimum) statement for an r−3 potential did not happen: all seven signs are negative.

What this is not. Not a statement about real excitons, bilayers, moiré devices or any material; no melting, no structural transition, no instability claim; not a global statement. It concerns the harmonic zero-point energy of a model crystal in model units.

Tier split. Tier A (Lean 4.34.1, pinned Mathlib; the theorems of Programmes.ZeroPointDipolar.Basic, namely the logic and the signs of rational endpoints; the generic window lemmas are N2's ZeroPointPhys and are reused; axioms within propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, e.g. 'ProgZeroPointDipolar.riesz3_not_localMin_of_certificate' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; leanchecker replay rc 0, run by the producer; the final theorems are conditional on the non-kernel inputs). Tier C-ball (Arb ball arithmetic, not kernel-checked): enclosures of the window curvature M for the seven potentials ([-3.17029, -1.66310] for Riesz 3; [-3.33620, -1.85185] and [-5.38812, -4.11598] for d = 1/10 and 1/2; [-3.23699, -1.74649], [-3.32496, -1.84069], [-3.36115, -1.88023], [-5.49473, -4.24958] for d/a = 0.06, 0.09, 0.1, 0.5), each containing the Tier X value of E''(0); the Ewald-split certificate (short part in real space with incomplete-gamma closed forms and N2's shell tail lemma at Qmax 300; long part in reciprocal space with the exact Fourier transform 4 sqrt(pi alpha) exp(-x²/(4 alpha)) − 2 pi x erfc(x/(2 sqrt(alpha))), the k = 0 term and the first shell exact, the rest by rigorous Cauchy-estimate balls of at most 1.6e-10). Tier C-human: the written glue inherited from N2 and the new Ewald items (mixture representation, Poisson summation, Cauchy estimates, Voronoi integral lemmas). Tier X: floating-point scans and Lindemann ratios in model units.

Controls. Positive: Gaussian a = 1 [-8.23325, -7.15778]; Gaussian a = 2 and Yukawa kappa = 2 bit-identical to N2; Yukawa kappa = 1 [-4.16485, -2.03702] contains N2's interval but is not bit-identical; Ewald-specific point checks against an independent direct float sum. Negative: Gaussian a = 2 (M in [+3.4496, +4.4631]) not certified; r−3 without the split refused by the tail lemma; a false Lean certificate fails to compile (rc 1); planted sorry and axiom caught by the axiom gate. Weakness: the reciprocal-space code has no negative control of its own and is validated only by the other checks.

Status. Written by AI agents under the author's direction. No independent audit (AI or human) exists at writing; the independent kernel replay and an independent re-run of the certificates are owed; no statement lock.
